top_risks_for_decomposition.summary: The zero-shared-database finding is bounded by this repository. If application_id d634afdb-97cc-4589-a080-5766d4f377d5 actually denotes a production system whose inventory state persists in a store owned by a DIFFERENT application, that store — and any cluster it sits on — is entirely invisible to a static walk of this tree and this artifact would understate coupling to zero.
top_risks_for_decomposition.why_it_matters: A false-negative shared-DB result is the failure mode that causes late wave slippage: co-waving constraints discovered after sequencing are the top cause of cutover rework. Every other conclusion in this artifact is conditional on this one.
top_risks_for_decomposition.mitigation: Obtain business-owner confirmation that this repository is the whole system and that no out-of-repo persistent store exists. Until confirmed, do not treat this application as unconstrained for wave-sequencing purposes.

top_risks_for_decomposition.summary: There is no executable behavioural baseline for the 75-line UpdateQuality() rules engine. The test assembly declares no ProjectReference to the console project and its single test asserts Assert.True(true), while UpdateQuality is an instance method on the internal class Program reading a private field — so the rules are mechanically unreachable from any other assembly.
top_risks_for_decomposition.why_it_matters: This platform's decisive-decomposition bias is explicitly conditional on the target being behaviour-verifiable. With zero coverage of the only business logic present, no data or logic cutover can be verified by replay, which removes the precondition the decisive path depends on.
top_risks_for_decomposition.mitigation: Make the rules reachable (extract to a referencable library with a public entry point), then pin today's OBSERVED behaviour with characterisation tests — including the unimplemented 'Conjured' rule and the self-cancelling 'Quality = Quality - Quality' branch — BEFORE any transformation.

open_questions: Does a persistent store exist outside this repository? The application has no durability, no audit trail and no record of a nightly inventory run, which is unusual for a system under portfolio management. If the real production system writes inventory to a database owned by another application, that store is invisible to this walk and this artifact's zero-cluster finding would not hold. This is RISK-01 and is the single question that most affects the result.

review_asks.title: Does this application store its inventory data anywhere outside its own code repository?
review_asks.why: If a production data store exists that this repository does not reference, it could sit on a shared database cluster and force this application into another application's migration wave — the opposite of the no-sharing conclusion recorded here.
review_asks.assessment: On the evidence in this repository the application has no database at all: it holds its six inventory items in memory, updates them once, and loses them when the process exits. It therefore shares no database with any other application and places no data-related constraints on migration scheduling. That conclusion is only valid if this repository is the entire system.
review_asks.reasoning: Four independent Discovery analyses and a first-hand sweep of all 22 tracked files agree: no connection string, no database driver, no ORM, no schema file, and no configuration section that could point at a database. The one signal that superficially suggests a data tier — a System.Data reference in the project file — is an unused Visual Studio template default with no matching code. The conflicting signal is contextual rather than technical: an application with no durability and no audit trail of its nightly run is an odd thing to find under portfolio management, which is why out-of-repository persistence is worth ruling out explicitly rather than assuming.

confidence.rationale: The absence is measured rather than assumed, verified first-hand, and corroborated by four upstream artifacts. Confidence is held below certainty only because static analysis cannot observe a store that the code does not reference.
